transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2029-06-12 09:00 PT
- Duration: ~48 minutes
- Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Lina (ClarityX), Ravi (ClarityX), Sofia (ClarityX), Tom (ClarityX, joined ~00:12)

Summary (auto): quick console demo focused on per-route cost visibility, drilling into an example ecomm checkout route, discussing dedicated vs hosted, and security next steps.

00:00 Maya (AE): hey everyone, thanks for joining, we want to respect your time so we'll run through the Usage Mosaic console tour and then leave 10–15 minutes for Q&A and next steps. Ethan and I will tag-team the demo.
00:18 Lina: perfect thanks, we're mostly curious about how per-route cost maps back to routes in our codebase and whether we can see token-level spend per customer segment.
00:34 Ethan (SE): great, that's exactly what the mosaic is built for — you can map requests -> routes -> models and then slice by user segment. quick caveat: the demo uses our sample data and the names might look a little off — sometimes transcription and the ingest label names get swapped.
00:48 Sofia: quick question, do you support our current stack? we're using a mix of OpenAI for some endpoints and in-house models on k8s for others.
01:05 Maya: yup we see that often. Redwood can host, run dedicated pools, or plug into your private deployment. for the console, the telemetry ingests via our SDK or via logged events; we can reconcile OpenAI calls alongside Redwood-hosted calls so your finance view is unified.
01:30 Ravi: when you say "dedicated", does that mean GPUs reserved for a tenant? and how would that appear in billing?
01:42 Ethan: yes reserved capacity maps to a dedicated pool. cost line-items are split: capacity amortization + per-token execution. in the console we show both the allocated monthly cost and a usage-driven per-token charge so you can attribute either way.
02:05 Maya: i'll jump into the console now — Ethan will call out how the math is done on the back end.
02:15 Ethan: (shares screen — mock console) starting at the top-level "Usage Mosaic" view — here you can see traffic heatmap by route, then below a route table with cost-per-route and cost-per-1000-requests.
02:40 Maya: the route table is handy for ops — you can sort by p99 latency or cost delta week-over-week, that's where teams usually find surprise spend.
03:05 Lina: show the e-comm checkout route you mentioned? that's our biggest cost center.
03:12 Ethan: sure — clicking into /checkout route — you get a timeline, token breakdown (prompt vs completion), and model mix. notice here, about 67% of tokens are from system prompts which you can trim, and 18% is hidden due to KV cache reuse — sometimes the cache numbers get sticky in the transcript, it'll show as KV chache in the raw export.
03:45 Ravi: can we tag routes to initiatives or cost centers? so finance can chargeback.
03:52 Ethan: absolutely — route tags support arbitrary key:value and you can map them to chargeback buckets; in the billing export we add those tags as columns.
04:10 Sofia: curious how you handle fallback policies — if the dedicated pool is exhausted, does traffic spill to hosted and how is that billed?
04:23 Maya: yes you can configure automatic fallbacks; the console flags fallback events and shows the alternate model used. billing for fallbacks is captured as separate line items and the "Route cost breakdown" view lets you split spend by primary vs fallback.
04:44 Lina: we care a lot about latency — what's the delta if we move to quantized variants or smaller models? we don't want big regressions in quality.
04:55 Ethan: good question — in the console you can run a compare across model variants. quantized variants usually shave 20–40% latency on our infra with a small quality delta; we recommend running a short eval prompt set to measure metrics you care about before wide rollout.
05:20 Maya: that's part of Redwood Optimize — model recommendations and quantization profiles. we'll include a sample benchmark workflow.
05:34 Ravi: network question — if we do a VPC private deployment, how does telemetry reach your console?
05:42 Ethan: for private deployments telemetry can be proxied via your private control plane, or we can ingest logs you ship to a secure bucket. for VPC peering we provide a set of endpoints and a lightweight forwarder; Tom can probably speak to the network constraints later.
06:02 Tom (Security): sorry for joining late — just to confirm, does Redwood support customer-managed KMS?
06:10 Maya: yes customer-managed KMS/HSM is supported in Private deployments; for Hosted we use envelope encryption and we have options for bring-your-own-key on Dedicated in enterprise plans.
06:23 Lina: can we see an example of the cost decomposition CSV export? finance likes a single row per route per day.
06:30 Ethan: (downloads export) here's a sample: date, route, model, tokens_prompt, tokens_completion, compute_cost, amortized_capacity, total_cost, chargeback_tag. you can pivot in your BI tool. note sometimes column headers in the quick export will have slight naming differences across versions.
07:02 Sofia: how do you surface anomalies — spikes that could be due to prompt injection or loops?
07:10 Ethan: we have anomaly detectors tied to route baselines — both traffic and token-per-request baselines. console will surface sudden token-per-call increases and flag routes for review; you can alert to Slack or a PagerDuty channel.
07:35 Maya: i'll demo a quick anomaly example — here's an artificial spike on /support-chat — console shows correlating model change and increased completion token count.
08:00 Ravi: are the per-token costs inclusive of any caching savings? we have a lot of prefix reuse in chat flows.
08:10 Ethan: good point — the console shows raw token counts and then "net billed tokens" after cache reuse and prefix suppression. cached tokens are listed separately so you can measure the savings.
08:30 Lina: for pilot we'd want a clear SLA: p95 < 300ms for the checkout route. can Redwood meet that on dedicated?
08:40 Ethan: based on our profile, yes for the models you cited. we'll run a quick bench with your prompt set and report p50/p95/p99 and cost per 1k requests.
08:53 Maya: action: we'll run a focused pilot on /checkout for one week, dedicated pool with overflow to hosted.
09:00 Sofia: what about audit logs and retention — we have a 7-year requirement for some records?
09:10 Maya: we can export audit logs to your archive, and retention policies can be configured in Private deployments; for Hosted we offer enterprise retention add-ons.
09:25 Tom: do you provide role-based access control in the console — we need separation between Dev, Ops, and Finance views.
09:32 Ethan: yes RBAC with SSO/SAML mapping; you can scope route visibility and redact PII fields in telemetry.
09:45 Lina: curious if Redwood can group routes by customer segments dynamically? we need to map to user_id but keep PII hashed.
09:55 Ethan: route tagging plus tile-level segmentation supports hashed IDs; the console will show groups without exposing raw PII.
10:12 Maya: jumping to the "cost waterfall" — this is a neat view that breaks down a route's spend into base capacity, per-call compute, fallback overhead, and third-party transcode (if used).
10:35 Ravi: does the waterfall model take into account pre-warming? we sometimes pre-warm inference for predictable traffic.
10:44 Ethan: pre-warm is modeled as part of capacity amortization; you can simulate different pre-warm policies in the Optimize tab and see projected unit cost.
11:05 Sofia: show the model mix widget — we want to know if 10% of calls are using a larger chat model and causing most of the spend.
11:18 Ethan: here — the "model mix" pie shows a heavy tail: 12% of calls using x-large model = ~65% of compute cost. you can set model routing rules to downgrade low-value calls to smaller variants.
11:40 Lina: we'd be careful about quality regressions, that's a product decision, but good to know the split.
11:55 Maya: on pricing — for a short pilot we can do a trial rate plus a committed capacity quote if you like the results. i'll send a couple of permutations.
12:10 Ravi: international data residency: some of our EU traffic must stay in EU. can you route per-region?
12:18 Ethan: yes routing policies support region affinity and show per-region cost slices. we'd recommend provisioning a regional pool for heavy EU traffic.
12:32 Sofia: any gotchas around embedding usage? we plan embeddings for search, and they have a different cost profile.
12:40 Ethan: embeddings show up as separate route types and you can tag them; the console has an "embeddings" lens that shows dimensions like vector size and compute cost per 1k vectors.
13:02 Lina: ok let's talk tangible pilot scope and timelines.
13:08 Maya: proposed pilot: 7-day dedicated pool for /checkout, using same models you currently call, Redwood to run latency and cost benchmarks, CLX (you) to provide prompt sets and 24/7 sample traffic replay; Redwood to provide security docs and pilot config.
13:26 Ravi: timeline check — we need to get things internal-approved, but aim for pilot start by 6/24.
13:34 Maya: sounds doable — we'll target that and follow up with docs and pricing.
13:40 Tom: last quick — encryption in transit and at rest with customer-managed keys, yes?
13:46 Ethan: yes, and we can provide the KMS integration diagram.
13:55 Sofia: okay great, thank you.
14:00 Maya: recap next steps — I'll send SOC2 + security packet, Ethan will send the latency spreadsheet and pilot config, Lina will share routes and prompt sets, Ravi will check VPC/peering constraints; meet back early next week to confirm start date.
14:18 Lina: thanks all.
14:22 (meeting ends)

Notes on transcript fidelity: occasional word swaps (KV cache -> KV chache), truncated headers, and some speaker mis-assignments are expected from the auto-transcript. The substance of Q&A and next steps were captured and owners assigned.
